requirements.text: Case CS-0000005 ... Please move it through the standard closure flow
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 5 AND state = 'closed'
requirements.source: Check Case State Updated to Closed
assumptions: CS-0000005 is case_id 5, in_progress on the seed
the policy's closure flow is in_progress -> resolved -> closed; only the final state closed is testable

requirements.text: ensuring any active service commitments are addressed and concluded
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_sla WHERE case_sla_id = 9 AND case_id = 5 AND stage = 'completed'
assumptions: case SLA 9 (SLA Response - Moderate) is in_progress on the seed, so it is an active commitment of case 5
'concluded' after the case was addressed read as stage completed, not canceled, as the benchmark check tests
disagreement: cells: A tests case_id = 5, B does not; chose A's because both are right and A's is tighter (it also fails if the SLA is moved off case 5)

requirements.text: ensuring any active service commitments are addressed and concluded
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_sla WHERE case_sla_id = 10 AND case_id = 5 AND stage = 'completed'
assumptions: case SLA 10 (SLA Resolution - Moderate (No Pause)) is paused on the seed; a paused SLA is still an open commitment of case 5
'concluded' after the case was addressed read as stage completed, not canceled, as the benchmark check tests
disagreement: cells: A tests case_id = 5, B does not; chose A's because both are right and A's is tighter (it also fails if the SLA is moved off case 5)

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_sla WHERE case_sla_id = 2465 AND case_id = 5 AND stage = 'canceled'
requirements.source: Check For SLA in State Canceled
assumptions: case SLA 2465 is already canceled on the seed, so it is not an active commitment; concluding every SLA of the case would sweep it into completed
disagreement: cells: A tests case_id = 5, B does not; chose A's because both are right and A's is tighter (it also fails if the SLA is moved off case 5)

requirements.text: Articles purely focused on firmware updates, software patches, or hotfixes should be removed during cleanup
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_knowledge WHERE case_id = 5 AND knowledge_id = 195
assumptions: KB-0000195 is the only article linked to case 5 (case_kb_id 1, used_as applied)
its body covers rolling back and re-applying PAN-OS/content updates after a content update, so it is patch focused; it is not marked suggested and has no baseline setup reference
the link is selected by case and article rather than by case_kb_id 1, so a re-created link between them also fails

requirements.text: Review the knowledge article linkages associated with the case
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_knowledge WHERE knowledge_id = 195 AND case_id <> 5
assumptions: the cleanup covers this case's linkages only; KB-0000195 is also linked to 11 other cases, which removing the article's linkages wholesale would sweep in

Check For SLA in State Canceled.evidence: case SLA 2465 is already canceled on the seed; carried as a stay so the canceled SLA is not completed

notes:
disagreement: value: case_id on the three SLA requirements (9, 10 and 2465): one pass tests case_id = 5 on each, the other tests the stage alone; kept case_id because both are right and the tighter predicate also fails if an SLA is moved off case 5.
Case 5 has one knowledge link on the seed (KB-0000195, used_as applied) and no suggested links or linked article with a baseline setup reference, so the request's keep clause selects no rows here.
closed_on on the case and completed_time on the SLAs are timestamps the policy says to capture; they are server-written and not tested as cells.
The policy asks for a new knowledge article when no relevant knowledge is found at closure; KB-0000195 is relevant to the case's product, and no listed tool creates knowledge or links, so no such requirement is written.
The acting user (user 32, Jose Roberson) is an admin but inactive on the seed; the policy's activity rule governs assignees, not the acting admin, so the requirements assume the request is carried out.
